title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion in Order Service
description: Order service exhausts its database connection pool due to a connection leak in a new error handling path. Connections are not returned to pool when a downstream inventory service call fails. Pool saturation causes all database operations to timeout.
initial_symptoms: Order service database queries timing out

evidence_catalog.summary: Database connection pool usage for order-service increased from 40% to 100% over 10 minutes
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT max(db_connection_pool_used) FROM metrics WHERE service='order-service'
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate connection pool metrics showing gradual saturation

evidence_catalog.summary: HikariCP log: 'Pool exhausted - Timeout waiting for connection after 30000ms'
evidence_catalog.query_reference: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE service='order-service' AND message LIKE '%Pool exhausted%'
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate HikariCP pool exhaustion logs

evidence_catalog.summary: Traces show order-service calls inventory-service which times out, then DB connection not released
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate traces showing inventory timeout followed by missing connection close

evidence_catalog.summary: Inventory service call latency p99 increased from 200ms to 30s (timeout) starting at 14:30 UTC
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will generate HTTP client metrics for inventory-service calls

evidence_catalog.summary: Commit added try-catch for inventory call but forgot to close DB connection in catch block
evidence_catalog.synthetic_fixture_note: Phase 1/2 will create commit diff showing missing connection.close() in catch block

evidence_catalog.summary: Deployment deploy-790 rolled out order-service v1.4.2 at 14:00 UTC (30 min before incident)

changes.summary: Deployed order-service v1.4.2 with new inventory error handling

causal_chain.from_description: Deployment of order-service v1.4.2 with connection leak in error handling
causal_chain.to_description: Inventory service timeout triggers catch block that fails to return DB connection to pool

causal_chain.from_description: Connections leaked on each inventory timeout

causal_chain.to_description: All order-service DB operations timeout, HTTP 503 returned

contributing_factors: No pool usage alerting until exhaustion

misleading_or_confounding_signals: Database CPU also elevated (symptom of queued queries, not cause)
Inventory service had its own incident (but order-service leak is the root cause)

required_checks.description: Verify pool usage correlates with inventory timeouts
required_checks.expected_outcome: Pool usage increases exactly when inventory latency spikes

required_checks.description: Check commit for missing connection.close() in catch block
Analyze traces for connection leak pattern
required_checks.expected_outcome: Traces show inventory timeout followed by no connection release

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Add try-with-resources or finally block to ensure connection is returned to pool
test_plan: Add unit test simulating inventory timeout
Load test with simulated inventory failures
Monitor pool usage in staging under failure injection
